The centre brings together researchers, industry and public partners to develop AI applications for the maritime sector. The PhD project will develop AI methods for navigational situational awareness and risk-based route planning, with applications in safe navigation and wind-assisted propulsion. A key question is how maritime data can be used to assess navigational risk and inform route and speed choices, accounting for vessel capabilities and uncertainty in the available information. The work will draw on two of the center's use cases: AI-driven S-100 electronic navigational chart products (UC3) and wind-assisted propulsion (UC5). UC3 concerns the use of electronic navigational chart data to assess hazards along a vessel's path. The use case will investigate how these assessments can account for the vessel's position and motion, together with characteristics such as draught, stopping distance and maneuvering capabilities. Historical AIS tracks combined with chart data offer a basis for constructing and studying navigational situations. It is also a goal of the use case that these assessments should be explainable. That is, it should be possible to trace a warning or recommendation to the data and criteria that produced it. In UC5, the focus is on route and speed planning for vessels with wind-assisted propulsion. Taking advantage of wind conditions can reduce fuel consumption, but the benefits depend on the vessel's performance and the route it can safely follow. The use case will investigate both how forecasts of wind and other environmental conditions can be used in voyage planning, accounting for navigational and operational constraint, and how adaptations can be made underway, accounting for actual conditions. The two use cases link the assessment of individual navigational situations to planning over a longer voyage. The project will examine how uncertainty in data and forecasts affects these decisions, and how plans can be revised as conditions change. Method development will build on machine learning in combination with established models of vessel behavior and navigation. The choice of methods will be developed as part of the doctoral work. The candidate will work closely with industry and public partners in the centre. The PhD candidate will be supervised by Associate Professor Børge Rokseth. title: Post-Doc position: AI-Driven Robotic Experimentation for Controlling Metal Degradation
description_for_fit: Metal degradation can be a boon or a bane, depending on the application and on how well we can control it. A corroding car component is a safety risk. At the Department of Electrochemistry and Big Data we unravel degradation pathways of light metals used in structural applications, medical devices and aqueous batteries. For these applications, degradation can be controlled using tailored electrolyte additives. The chemical space of possible additives is virtually infinite, so we do not test one-by-one.
